report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward culinary/restaurant/food‑blog style text relative to Model A.

Reasoning:
- The difference concentrates in mid-to-late layers (especially L16–L25, strongest at positions 1–4), which typically encode high-level semantics—consistent with a domain/style shift rather than low-level token quirks.
- Logit-lens top tokens across these layers repeatedly surface tightly clustered culinary/food-blog vocabulary: “restaurant”, “Restaurant”, “Chef/chef”, “cooking/Cooking”, “baking”, “kitchen”, “Cafe/Café”, “Cake”, “microwave”, “Cook”, “magazine”, “blogs/blogger/blogging”, “Blog”, “Food”, “Kitchen”, along with listicle/website markers (“www”, “No”, numbers, “International”, “Professional”).
- This theme is persistent across positions 2–4 and layers 17–25 (e.g., L20–L23 pos2–4 are dominated by restaurant/chef/cooking/blog terms), indicating that B places more probability mass on this domain during continuation.
- Early layers show mixed tokens, but the strong, consistent culinary/blog cluster emerges from ~L16 onward.

Conclusion: The evidence supports a domain/style difference—Model B appears finetuned or more predisposed to produce culinary/restaurant/food‑blog (and related lifestyle/marketing) content compared to Model A.
